answer: Sybil resistance is a one-bench lacquer gate. An applicant reserves one numbered cutting bench and receives a sealed lead-screw whose metric thread is mill-stamped to that seat. Only that holder may mount a uniquely serialled blank and, at an unannounced tick, cut a one-shot whisper; graders match the groove's ridge to the official comparator plate, plus screw stamp, blank serial, and bench log. A shared bench, a reused blank, or a pressed playback is forfeited as one farm. N aliases cost N exclusive benches, N unique blanks, and N live cuts no single operator can stack in the same minute.
